housing-infrastructure.quote:
Amidst a national housing shortage, we’re opening the doors to build, baby, build right here in Michigan.

This year, we’re creating a Housing Opportunity Tax Credit that paves the way for building an extra 2,500 affordable units per year.

In my State of the State address earlier this year, I outlined my plan to make housing more accessible to Michiganders. I called for slashing red tape and creating a statewide affordable housing tax credit.

5 months later, I'm proud to say that we got it done.
This year, my budget includes funding for the Michigan Housing Opportunity Tax Credit, paving the way for 2,500 new or rehabilitated affordable units to be built annually.
We also cut red tape and barred large investors from buying up hundreds of homes, so that every Michigander has a path to homeownership.

Buying a home is tough enough, you shouldn’t have to compete with corporate landlords.

That's why we're preventing this from becoming a real problem in Michigan. Last week, I signed legislation that prohibits private equity from buying up hundreds of homes from working families.

Across the nation, housing shortages are driving up costs for working families. That’s why I signed new bills that cut red tape and modernize building codes, speeding up new construction and ensuring more families can call Michigan home.

The Gordie Howe bridge is proof that when we work together, we can get hard things done.

I made sure this bridge opened to deliver a better economic future for all. Everyone should be able to make it in Michigan.

state-local-politics.quote:
When I took office 7.5 years ago, growing Michigan’s economy responsibly was one of my top priorities.

Fast forward to 2026, and I’ve now signed 8 balanced, bipartisan budgets that have set Michigan up for a brighter future. Here’s why that matters. 👇

Together we've improved upon the state’s fiscal record by increasing the rainy-day fund, paying down debt, and strengthening Michigan’s credit rating.

Plus, we've invested in our schools, grown our economy, and lowered costs for Michiganders.
After 8 budgets, we’re leaving Michigan’s finances better than we found them.
